newsitem.title: USA: ALTEON GETS AGING DISEASE THERAPY PATENT.
newsitem.headline: ALTEON GETS AGING DISEASE THERAPY PATENT.

text.p: Alteon Inc said Tuesday that it has received a broad patent covering a novel class of compounds that could potentially treat diseases of aging.
Alteon said the patent covers A.G.E. cross-link breakers, which have the ability to break what were previously believed to be permanent, A.G.E.-mediated bonds between proteins.
A.G.E. cross-link breakers offer the possibility of the first therapeutic approach to remove A.G.E. cross-links, which are associated with many age-related diseases and the complications of diabetes.

Protein cross-links are formed as a result of a chemical reaction between proteins in the body and circulating blood glucose. These protein cross-links contribute to tissue and vascular damage, playing a fundamental role in clinical problems resulting from diabetes and aging.

Kidney disease, heart disease, cataracts, circulatory problems (sometimes requiring amputations), stroke and blindness are among the complications associated with protein cross-linking and the accumulation of A.G.E.s.
Alteon's lead compound, pimagedine, currently in Phase III human trials, inhibits the formation of A.G.E.s, thereby potentially delaying the cascade of complications of diabetes and aging.
